weekend_note: Sunny and dry all week: highs 71 today rising to the upper 70s by midweek, lows in the mid 50s, rain chance 2% or less through next weekend. Picks: UWF volleyball today at 1 PM, Blue Angels practice Tuesday, free Bands on the Beach Tuesday night, the Interstate Fair opening Thursday, Taste of Gulf Breeze Friday and Ice Flyers on Saturday (indoors at the Bay Center). Storm cancellations: Local Pulse's Oct 15 list showed Barktoberfest, Boo at the Zoo and the Sunday Market canceled for this weekend, so check before heading out. Escambia schools are preparing to reopen Monday.

news.title: One week after Isaias, tarps and debris line Pensacola streets
news.summary: Power is back for many homes, roofing crews are getting busier and crews are clearing big fallen trees. A wind advisory complicated cleanup, and the Forest Service asked residents not to burn debris.

news.title: Power largely restored; Escambia debris bill estimated near $55 million
news.summary: State officials said 95% of affected customers had power by Oct 14, down from about 450,000 outages at the peak. Escambia estimates $54.87 million for debris removal within a $64 million preliminary damage figure.

news.title: Escambia schools, UWF and Pensacola State set to resume Monday
news.summary: Public schools are preparing to reopen Oct 19, and UWF and Pensacola State classes resume that day. UWF's east entrance and nature trails stay closed, and its inauguration events were postponed.

news.title: SNAP replacement requests due Monday; last county-coordinated meal sites ran Oct 16
news.summary: Residents who lost food can request replacement benefits through the MyACCESS portal through Oct 19. 211 Northwest Florida remains available around the clock for food, housing and utility help.

news.title: Boil-water notices continue in Milton, Jay and Bagdad Garcon Point; Gulf Breeze resource fair Oct 23
news.summary: Navarre Beach's notice was lifted Oct 14, but City of Milton Water, the Town of Jay and Bagdad Garcon Point Water still have notices. The Navarre Chamber's recovery resource fair is Oct 23 at St. Sylvester Catholic Church in Gulf Breeze.

news.title: Local Pulse: shops reopen as businesses ask for weekend support
news.summary: The roundup points readers to local shops and cafes, including the Renfroe pecan shops reopening Oct 17 and Holland Farms' pumpkin patch. It warns that post-storm hours may vary and that many markets were canceled that weekend.

news.title: Escambia County debris pickup expected to take months
news.summary: Officials expect three to four months of cleanup with several rounds and warn against paying unlicensed yard workers. Carried over from the Oct 16 update.

coverage_note: Written overnight Sunday Oct 18. Temperatures are from WeatherBug and rain chances from Fox Weather (Oct 18 to 23) and The Weather Network (Oct 24 and 25); all show sunny, dry days. Many sites could not be opened (Visit Pensacola's event calendar, Saenger, Ice Flyers, Blue Wahoos, City of Pensacola, WEAR's news index, Pensacola News Journal), and NorthEscambia.com's homepage was stale and its events page could not be loaded, so Gonzalez, Molino and Beulah coverage is thin. Cantonment, Gonzalez and Barrineau Park items below carried over from the Allevents listing and were not rechecked; the Oct 17 ones have been dropped. Barktoberfest was removed and Boo at the Zoo flagged after Local Pulse's Oct 15 list showed them canceled. No restaurant openings were confirmed; Launch's own page lists an Oct 17 soft opening, while Pelican Bar and Grill and Casa Luvia remain unconfirmed. Ice Flyers, Wahoos, Bands on the Beach and most later events were carried over without a recheck. Most news comes from a WUWF live-updates page whose newest posts are dated Oct 16.
